newsitem.title: UK: Tightening supply boosts NWE spot gas oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Tightening supply boosts NWE spot gas oil prices.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices held a firmer tone on Tuesday with tightening ARA supplies creating some supportive buying interest for barges and steadying cargo premiums to firmer benchmark gas oil futures, traders said.
Brokers said prompt barge supplies were becoming fairly tight and although end-user demand was balanced trade house short-covering had boosted premiums by around 50 cents.
However, trade was thin with the small contango between July and August futures encouraging sellers to raise offers.
Prompt barges were bid up to around July IPE +$1 in early business but valued around July +$1 a tonne fob Rotterdam near the IPE close with no trade reported.

The market for second half July barge liftings was also slightly firmer, but brokers said buyers and sellers were at a stand-off with buyers at July IPE +50 cents finding sellers asking August IPE +$1 per tonne fob ARA.
Diesel barges were traded at a steady July IPE +$5 a tonne and were later talked around July IPE +$5/+$5.50 fob ARA with Flushing liftings discounted by around $1.
Diesel cargoes were not so stable though with values for prompt deliveries slipping around 50 cents to around July IPE +$4 a tonne cif Rotterdam.
